answer: Picture the trust graph as a lagoon: honest agents form a broad, well-linked basin, while a sybil swarm is a tight pool joined to it by only a few attack edges. Run short random walks seeded from verified agents and score each vertex by the walk mass landing on it, normalized by degree. However many fake accounts a raven-eyed attacker mints, they split the trickle crossing those few edges, so their combined rewards and votes stay capped.
